patch.value: Refuse a recursive promotion when any declared workflow unit regresses
Let a fixed evaluation plan bound the empirical regression of every correlation unit with one sealed declaration.

Check all complete paired units exactly in either objective direction before promotion and preserve independent approval and resource bounds.; Preserve legacy comparisons and fail closed on incomplete, changed or sequential guarded plans.; Measure masking and equivalent-plan token savings on seeded synthetic workflows through the SDK and CLI.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Ranked by value / (risk x effort), each dimension 1 to 5. Per-unit regression guard 5/(1x2)=2.50: current plan caps protected cohorts at 32 and a mean masks a single workflow loss. Learned context routing 5/(3x4)=0.42: existing public history-prefix task has 943 fit and 385 final items, but completion after choosing a projection lacks a counterfactual. Further meta-loop search 3/(3x4)=0.25: bounded recipe and proposer search already exist, with zero promotions in the published transfer replay. All three retain sealed limits, independent human approval and fail-closed lineage.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Implement optional max_unit_regression on fixed plans. Reuse exact decimal arithmetic on paired members within each declared correlation unit. Report one worst unit and the count in breach, keep earlier cohorts and aggregate gates effective, and retest persisted evidence and the authoritative promotion command.

value.author: pi-glm
value.text: Inventory of what already exists on main (PR #190, commit 1b3e965, plus the arithmetic fix 5353941): evaluation-plan.ts parses optional max_unit_regression on fixed plans (sequential+guard refuses eval_plan_stopping), evaluateUnitGuard checks every complete unit with exact rational paired means, direction-aware (maximize/minimize), inclusive limits, worst-unit tie-break on the smallest label, violations count; evaluatePlan overrides the verdict with code eval_unit_regression on any breach; validateEvaluationReport guards the emitted shape; verifyEvaluationScore propagates the typed refusal at promotion; CLI rl eval plan register/show/evaluate expose it (details include max_unit_regression and unit_guard), the promote command refuses with eval_unit_regression, and the README documents the seeded seed-42 study with a tiktoken table. Tests: test/worst-cohort.test.ts per-unit guard cases, test/fixtures/unit-guard-study.ts emits the raw three-plan comparison for external token counting. Remaining gaps in this slice: (1) the eval_unit_regression refusal and report reason do not name the worst unit, its two scores or the bound, so a refused promotion does not say why in one call; unit_guard carries only the signed improvement, not both per-unit means; (2) no exhaustive decision/transition table test (guard x complete x outcome x direction x plan changed/sequential); (3) the masking/token-savings measurement is not one reproducible script: the recorded README numbers were counted externally with tiktoken and the fixture only emits raw JSON, with no CLI-side measurement; (4) the rl eval plan register/evaluate --help descriptions do not mention the per-unit guard. I will close exactly these four gaps, preserving every existing behaviour.

value.text: Design of this slice (all four gaps closed, no existing behaviour weakened): (1) unit_guard now carries the worst unit's displayed candidate_mean and incumbent_mean alongside the existing improvement/bound/violations (exact rational decision arithmetic unchanged; validateEvaluationReport bounds both new means inside reward_bounds); (2) the eval_unit_regression verdict reason and the typed promotion refusal name the unit, both scores, the bound, the violation count and the shared sealed-design remedy, so one promote call states the cause (the SDK error-context contract is strictly typed, so the witness text lives in the message and context.why); (3) test/worst-cohort.test.ts gains the required transition/decision table (guard present/absent x complete/incomplete x improved/equal/regressed x maximize/minimize, plus changed-digest drift, sequential-with-guard refusal and preserved sequential-without-guard) and a CLI help-surface test; (4) test/unit-guard-measure.ts is the one-command reproducible measurement: build, npm pack, install the exact archive into a fresh non-git scratch tracker, replay the seeded 42 study through the SDK and the real pm CLI (JSON and TOON) in both directions, and count o200k_base tokens with the new pinned devDependency js-tiktoken 1.0.21. value.author: pi-glm
value.text: Re-review round 1, blocking finding fixed (class closed, not the line). Rule violated: displayed diagnostic means must be correctly rounded exact sums, never running float averages that cancel. Instances found and fixed: (1) the per-unit guard's candidate_mean, incumbent_mean and improvement and (2) the protected-cohort improvement both ran incremental float averages (evaluateUnitGuard/evaluateCohorts over unitDifferences); both now derive from exact rational per-unit sums through a new roundRationalMean wrapper that pre-scales decimals into subnormal units before the sealed roundFloatMean core, so the reviewer's case (candidate [1e16, 0, -1e16] vs incumbent [1e16, 1, -1e16]) reports candidate mean 0, incumbent mean 0.3333333333333333, improvement -0.3333333333333333 instead of three zeros. (3) validateEvaluationReport's improvement domain compared against the float subtraction hi - lo, which is one ulp TIGHTER than the exact reward width (0.3 - 0.1 = 0.19999999999999998 vs the exact 0.2), falsely refusing legitimate correctly rounded values; the bound is now the correctly rounded exact width (monotone rounding keeps every produced improvement inside it). Searched the package for other instances: the aggregate top-level candidate_mean/incumbent_mean reconstruction and the sequential boundary means are decision-bearing sealed legacy comparisons, deliberately unchanged here (preserve legacy comparisons) and already tracked by pm-rl-aggregate-mean-precision from the previous round. New tests: the reviewer's adversarial case in both directions plus a seeded property loop (4-member units, even-integer rows below 2^15 magnitude and a small offset loss, BigInt-sum oracle, exact /4 dyadic means) covering the guard and cohort report paths. Revert proof: with the pre-fix product code the two new tests fail 0/2 (improvement trial 0 assertion plus the adversarial case); with the fix restored they pass 2/2 and the whole worst-cohort quick file passes 16/16.
